default_exit._why: one exit for every family so rules compete on the same footing; the owner will decide the demo stop/take-profit later and this block changes then (a change = a new screen run, its variants counted again)
default_exit._fills: signal at the close of bar t; market order at the open of the 1-minute bar that starts at t's close (+ slippage); every 1-minute bar from the entry minute on: stop first (fills at the stop or the gap open, - slippage), then the target (a limit: needs a trade 1 tick through, fills at the target); time exit at the open of the first minute at or after entry + max_hold_min; flat at the session's flatten time; one position at a time; at most max_entries_per_session entries per session

E-548.title: Multi-horizon stretch agreement fade
E-548.hypothesis: When the 1x, 2x and 4x horizon returns are all stretched the same way in volatility units, late chasers have pushed the index beyond what liquidity providers need; the next 30 minutes tend to give part back.

E-549.title: Persistence-regime bar-break follow
E-549.hypothesis: When the rolling lag-1 return autocorrelation is positive (orders are being sliced and executed in one direction), a close beyond the previous bar's extreme is more likely to continue than to bounce.

E-550.title: Clock-block colour streak exhaustion fade
E-550.hypothesis: After several consecutive clock-aligned blocks of the same colour, the participants who wanted that direction are done; fade the move at the block close that completes the streak.

E-551.title: Schaff-style double-stochastic MACD turn follow
E-551.hypothesis: Stochastic of a stochastic of the MACD gives an early, bounded cycle signal; a cross out of the low zone marks the start of a push that momentum followers extend.

E-552.title: Gap-bar reversal toward the prior close
E-552.hypothesis: A bar that opens far from the previous close (stops or a large market order) and closes back against the gap shows the impulse had no follow-up; the gap tends to fill.

E-553.title: Efficiency-collapse trend-end fade
E-553.hypothesis: A very efficient (one-way) run followed by a collapse of the path-efficiency ratio means the one-sided flow has stopped; price tends to revert toward the middle of the run.

E-554.title: TRIX zero-cross follow
E-554.hypothesis: The one-bar rate of change of a triple-smoothed EMA filters out noise; its zero cross marks a persistent change of direction that trend followers act on.

E-555.title: Block-end extreme close fade
E-555.hypothesis: A clock block that is wide for its length and closes at its own extreme was driven by late urgency; the next block usually retraces part of it.

E-556.title: Range-top dwell then slip fade
E-556.hypothesis: After price has sat at the top (bottom) of its rolling range for several minutes, the first clear slip back shows buyers (sellers) gave up; the dwell was distribution, so follow the slip.

E-557.title: Single-bar VWAP slice follow
E-557.hypothesis: One large bar that opens on one side of the session VWAP and closes on the other, on above-average volume, is an institutional shift of the day's average price; follow it.
